clue.text: Brave ? The opposite — and looks it!

definitions.text: Brave ? The opposite — and looks it!

parts.words: Brave ? The opposite — and looks it!
parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior; the opposite, in old Western slang, was a white settler, whose face looked pale

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a courageous person and their contrary appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: In Westerns a white settler was named by Native Americans for skin lighter than their own, the counterpart of a brave.

clue.text: Peremptory advice to choose the French preserve

parts.note: a curt order to choose is 'pick!'
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone bossily telling another to pick the French jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinegar-cured relish is a kind of preserve.

clue.text: Ruling over the seamy side ?

explanation.surface: A judgement made about the shady part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling paper means drawing lines on it; a garment's inner layer is the side where the seams show.

clue.text: Give the word to pass by a quaker

explanation.surface: A Quaker gives a password to get through.
explanation.walkthrough: A sentry's challenge 'Who goes there?' was answered 'Friend', so the word lets you pass. Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional reply to a sentry is this word, and a member of the Society of Friends is called one.

clue.text: Northern youth on rampage; call round local government HQ

indicators.note: round says the first word's letters surround the scrambled group

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a youth on the rampage runs wild, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A northern lad runs riot and is summoned to the council offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on rampage' scrambles N and YOUTH into OUNTYH, which 'round' places inside CALL. The printed '11' is stray noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The building where an English shire's council meets is the headquarters of local administration.

clue.text: Meet when Prince holds string of pearls

indicators.note: one thing holding another contains it, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: a long necklace of pearls is called a rope

explanation.surface: A prince holding a pearl necklace at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet in its old sense means fitting or suitable, a synonym.

clue.text: Practise what to say about a late carrier

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a vehicle carrying the late, the dead, is a hearse

explanation.surface: Someone running over a speech about a delayed courier.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors go over their lines in advance before a performance.

clue.text: Gathered duck peer about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone collected a duck that was peering around.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric drawn into small folds is said to be gathered.

clue.text: Inflame with a fresh match ?

parts.note: setting something alight again with a new matchstick, or reviving passion with a new partner

explanation.surface: Someone stirring up feeling with a new pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle again is to set burning once more, as with a new match.

clue.text: Persevere once unit disbands

indicators.note: a unit that disbands breaks up, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Keep going even after the squad breaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to carry on, a synonym.

clue.text: Child, I repeat, it's rather fussy and pretentious

indicators.note: repeat says the pair of pieces appears twice in a row

explanation.surface: A child is told to say something again because it sounds affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi describes showy, affectedly elegant style, a synonym of fussy pretension.

clue.text: No short memorandum, and the singer must hold on to it

definitions.text: the singer must hold on to it

explanation.surface: A lengthy message that a vocalist clings to.
explanation.definitionFit: A lengthy written message is not brief; a sustained sound is one a vocalist holds.

clue.text: Public spirited place

parts.note: a public house where spirits are served, not a civic-minded spot

explanation.surface: A community-minded location.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or pub is a public house serving spirits.

clue.text: That petrified look when a viewer seems not to recognise one

definitions.text: That petrified look when a viewer seems not to recognise one

parts.words: That petrified look when a viewer seems not to recognise one
parts.note: a blank fixed gaze, turned to stone in the pun on petrified, that refuses to acknowledge someone

explanation.surface: Someone frightened gazes at a person as though a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, blank fixed gaze, as if made of rock, ignores whoever is looked at.

clue.text: Why be scared to look as this paper is apparently blank?

definitions.text: Why be scared to look as this paper is apparently blank?

parts.words: Why be scared to look as this paper is apparently blank?
parts.note: the frightened go pale as linen, and an unprinted page is plain and colourless

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why a blank page frightens them.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightened face is pale as bedding, and a blank page is plain paper.

clue.text: Did the farmer win it for harvesting under an oak tree?

definitions.text: Did the farmer win it for harvesting under an oak tree?

parts.words: Did the farmer win it for harvesting under an oak tree?
parts.note: a trophy for grain harvesting, read as the little cupule holding an oak's nut beneath the tree

explanation.surface: A farmer's harvest prize found beneath an oak.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaly cupule that holds an oak nut, read as a trophy for grain.

clue.text: First personal statement that one carries goods, made abroad

definitions.text: First personal statement that one carries goods, made abroad

parts.note: a statement in the first person begins 'I am', contracted
a porter is one who carries loads

explanation.surface: A trader declares themselves a carrier of foreign goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader bringing in foreign-made goods effectively says 'I am a carrier' of them.

clue.text: Now, now, I beg you to attend

explanation.surface: Someone soothing and inviting another along.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a soothing remonstrance and a repeated plea to approach use the same doubled word.

clue.text: Vulgar comedown? You can't put me off it

definitions.text: You can't put me off it

parts.note: vulgar in its old sense means ordinary or common
to come down from the air is to land

explanation.surface: A crude humiliation, and a speaker who refuses to be shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can't put me off it' is spoken by a public field: no one can be turned off ground everyone has rights over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground shared by the community cannot be closed to a member of the public.

clue.text: Peculiar cigar left — because it has a pungent smell ?

indicators.note: 'has' puts one piece inside the other
peculiar means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd cigar was abandoned because it stank.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulb used in cooking is notorious for its strong odour.

clue.text: Went ahead after a day's date got muddled

indicators.note: after places the leading piece behind the others

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for day
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A diary entry for a day got confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that rot or wits that become confused are said to have gone bad in this way.

clue.text: Timothy shown up to be bashful about where he does forgery

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: bashful means shy

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up reads the name from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A shy man called Timothy is exposed as a counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' turns TIM into MIT, and 'about' puts SHY around it. 'Forgery' is the blacksmith's work at the forge, not counterfeiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's workshop is where metal is forged.

clue.text: Crooked, caught out, fleeced

indicators.note: out says the letter is removed

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A dishonest person is caught and swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheated or swindled is to be fleeced, a synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps a pen mother can bring more power to Egypt

definitions.text: can bring more power to Egypt

parts.note: a pen is a female swan, so a pen is perhaps a swan
dam is a mother, of an animal

explanation.surface: A writing pen and a mother energising Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: The barrage on the Nile at Aswan generates hydroelectric power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile barrage generates hydroelectricity for the country.

clue.text: A kind of lemon tonic mixture is about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
a mixture stirs things together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lemon in a tonic drink is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' turns TONIC into CITON, which goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is a large thick-skinned citrus resembling a lemon.

clue.text: Stumble at length on "Autumn section of stage scenery

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
a flat is a painted panel of theatre scenery

explanation.surface: Tripping over a piece of autumnal stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down full length is to tumble prostrate.

clue.text: Knock back and get plastered?

definitions.note: the clue's past form; the answer is the verb to plaster, and the question mark flags the looseness

indicators.note: back says the word for knock is read in reverse

parts.note: to rap is to knock

explanation.surface: Someone knocks back drinks and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAP into PAR. 'plastered' looks like drunk; it means coated with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Parget means to coat a wall with ornamental render.

clue.text: A box of potty refreshment

parts.note: a container for the drink brewed in a pot, not something crazy

explanation.surface: A crate of mad snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The canister holding the leaves brewed in a pot.
